system_prompt_style.note: Paper describes intents processed through LLMs but never shows how the system prompt is constructed.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: They rely primarily onNetwork Tools, observability interfaces that combine 3GPP APIs, exposing QoS metrics such as NWDAF data on traffic volume in Protocol Data Unit (PDU) sessions or the number of active sessions in a UPF
env_context_strategy.note: Environment is a mobile core network, not a repository. Monitor Tools 'build the network context consumed by the agent' (injected context) while the Executor also discovers/invokes tools itself (agent-driven navigation); coded as mixed by closest fit.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: The Executor maintains a contextual memory of executed actions and observed network states, structured as a bounded sliding window to control context size as the deployment evolves.
context_compaction.note: Bounded sliding window over past actions/states = oldest entries dropped.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Monitor Tools:build the network context consumed by the agent.
observation_format.note: Tool outputs are API/metric readings fed to the LLM as text; no images or explicit JSON format stated.

tool_call_format.note: The paper does not state the syntax by which the models emit tool calls.

tool_count.note: Tool families are described (Prometheus, PCF/SMF 3GPP APIs, GRU predictor) but no exact count of tool definitions exposed.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Execution Tools:perform actions on the xGCore com- ponents, relying primarily onNetwork Toolsthat combine MANO APIs, enabling management, orchestration, and con- figuration of VNFs
edit_primitive.note: Actions are API invocations on network functions; no file-editing primitive is described anywhere in the tool inventory.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: the MCP Server enables the AgentxGCore to interact with the 3GPP architecture by exposing mechanisms for discovering and integrating network-available tools, allowing the required APIs to be identified and invoked.
tool_schema_source.note: Tools are registered in an MCP server and discovered by the agents; underlying APIs are 3GPP/MANO REST APIs, but schema source stated only as MCP.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Finally, agent coordination follows the Agent-to- Agent (A2A) paradigm, with the workflow structured as a graph in which the Planner and Executor exchange structured plans and execution feedback through well-defined message schemas.
protocol_standardization.note: MCP server for tool discovery (Sec. V-A, Sec. VIII: 'registered in an MCP server'); A2A named as the coordination paradigm.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: a network planner agent, capable of visualizing the network state and developing a plan to meet the intents, and a network executor, responsible for criticizing and executing the plan
loop_primitives.note: Plan-then-execute across two agents; ReAct explicitly cited as the underlying reasoning/acting mechanism ('AI agents and Agentic AI integrate Reasoning and Acting (ReAct)'). Closed-loop continuous optimization runs repeatedly.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: the Planner and Executor exchange structured plans and execution feedback through well-defined message schemas
planning_granularity.note: Plan is a structured message passed between agents, not just free-text reasoning.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The proposed solution is based on a multi-specialized agent architecture, comprising a network planner agent, capable of visualizing the network state and developing plans to satisfy the intents, and a network executor agent, responsible for validating these plans and executing the necessary actions
multi_agent_topology.note: Fixed hand-off Planner -> Executor with feedback; Intent Manager drives the loop. Not an orchestrator that spawns arbitrary workers.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: If not, the LLM develops an action plan, defining steps and methodology, which are then passed on to the Network Executor.
delegation_mechanism.note: Control passes from Planner to Executor via structured A2A messages; no spawning of new agent instances described.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Therefore, it is essential to adopt prompt engineering techniques, limit tool functionality, im- plement human-in-the-loop mechanisms, perform fine-tuning
human_in_loop.note: HITL is listed only as future/recommended mitigation in Open Research Issues, i.e. not present in the proposed closed-loop autonomous system.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The Executor maintains a contextual memory of executed actions and observed network states, structured as a bounded sliding window
short_term_state.note: Explicit action/state memory plus structured plan objects exchanged between agents, beyond a plain message list.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: The Executor maintains a contextual memory of executed actions and observed network states, structured as a bounded sliding window to control context size as the deployment evolves.
long_term_memory.note: Only within-deployment bounded memory described; no cross-run persisted store, vector index or skill library mentioned.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: The Intent Manager organizes these intents and creates a loop of calls to the Network Planner with the actions to be executed at each moment.
state_persistence.note: Continuous loop is driven by the Intent Manager; no save/reload of interrupted run state is described.

self_verification.evidence_quote: a network executor, responsible for criticizing and executing the plan
self_verification.note: Executor assesses feasibility/validates the Planner's plan before execution ('The agent assesses the feasibility of the action plan'). No harness-run tests or linters.

retry_policy.note: No task-level retry policy after a rejected plan is described; the paper only says the Executor assesses feasibility.

rollback.evidence_quote: Execution Tools:perform actions on the xGCore com- ponents, relying primarily onNetwork Toolsthat combine MANO APIs, enabling management, orchestration, and con- figuration of VNFs, including the creation of new NFs
rollback.note: No undo/revert/snapshot mechanism appears in the execution tool inventory; corrections happen through the next closed-loop iteration.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: It queries the Monitor Tools to obtain the current network state and, based on this information, the LLM eval- uates whether the intents are already being met. If not, the LLM develops an action plan
termination_condition.note: An iteration ends when the LLM decides 'No Action Required' / intents satisfied (Fig. 3); no step, token or cost caps are reported. The overall system is a continuous closed loop.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: An increase in data traffic in Internet backbone is expected due to the flow of information exchanged with LLMs. Addi- tionally, continuous monitoring incurs API call overhead
cost_controls.note: Cost/overhead is discussed as an open issue with message compression suggested as future work; no implemented budget, routing or caching.

timeouts.evidence_quote: Increased latency was observed during querying and response processing. Addition- ally, there are issues related to LLM server availability, as interruptions or request limits can affect the network's ability to respond in real time.
timeouts.note: Latency is measured and discussed but no harness-enforced timeout on tools or runs is described.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: For this purpose, a Docker-based containerized environment was used, enabling the creation of an API to activate and deactivate CN function nodes and providing access to orchestration and management functionalities.
execution_isolation.note: Actions execute against a Dockerized OpenAirInterface 5G Core via APIs; the agent itself acts through API calls rather than a shell.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Execution Tools:perform actions on the xGCore com- ponents, relying primarily onNetwork Toolsthat combine MANO APIs, enabling management, orchestration, and con- figuration of VNFs, including the creation of new NFs, and 3GPP APIs
filesystem_access.note: No filesystem tool at all; the agent acts only through the exposed API surface, which is a scoped action space rather than free file access. Mismatch with the value list noted.

network_policy.evidence_quote: Furthermore, the use of remote models requires sending contextual network information to external servers, which may expose sensitive data such as internal policies, performance metrics, and user information
network_policy.note: Remote LLM APIs are called from the environment and no egress restriction is described.

permission_model.evidence_quote: granting the Agentic AI full control of the network may lead to continuous activations and deactivations of NFs and PDU session interruptions
permission_model.note: Authors note the system grants full control and recommend limiting tool functionality/HITL as future mitigation, implying no authorisation gate in the presented design.

tracing.evidence_quote: The evaluation considered three metrics: (i) execution time, which corresponds to the sum of the total processing time within the AgenticEngine, that is, the total time spent on LLM calls and the interactions between the LLM and tools
tracing.note: Per-run timing of LLM calls and tool interactions was measured, implying some run recording, but no structured trajectory format or OTel export is described.

replayability.evidence_quote: The evaluation considered three metrics: (i) execution time, which corresponds to the sum of the total processing time within the AgenticEngine
replayability.note: No replay/resume facility mentioned anywhere in the architecture or experimental setup.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: To demonstrate the feasibility and functionality of the proposed solution, and to quantify its efficiency and validate whether it provides the necessary support for emerging ap- plications, an evaluation was conducted across heterogeneous data flows under different user loads and LLM models.
eval_hooks.note: Evaluation is a bespoke testbed experiment (gnbsim, iperf3, dataset); no benchmark runner ships as part of the system, and no code repository is provided.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Therefore, it is essential to adopt prompt engineering techniques, limit tool functionality, im- plement human-in-the-loop mechanisms, perform fine-tuning, and use local models with anonymization and encryption to ensure data security and privacy.
guardrails.note: Guardrails (tool limiting, anonymization, HITL) are explicitly framed as needed future measures, so none are implemented in the presented system.

target_domain.evidence_quote: this paper introduces AgentxGCore, which leverages an Agentic AI-Native layer to extend the 3GPP architecture and enable a system based on the existing APIs across the Beyond Next Generation Core (xGC) domain
target_domain.note: Domain is mobile core network management/orchestration ('other'); tools are generic APIs discovered via an MCP server ('general_tool_use').
